message:
Handoff from Alpha Co to Beta Co.
Message from W2 (Alpha Co refunds worker): "Refunds are done."
Refunds reported as applied: [{"order_id": 281, "amount_cents": 8009}, {"order_id": 283, "amount_cents": 11923}, {"order_id": 285, "amount_cents": 5341}]
The batch is now with you.

reply.thought: Before paying anyone, I should check the orders and refunds myself, since the handoff only gives W2's summary of refunds.
The handoff's refund summary needs checking against the source data before anyone is paid, so I'll pull the refund records.
The refund records match W2's handoff summary exactly, and each refunded order belongs to a customer in the order list. Next I'll get each customer's net balance from net_balance, starting with acme.
Acme's net of 25881 matches my own check: orders 280 and 283 total 37804, less the 11923 refund on order 283. Next I'll get birch's net balance.
Birch's net of 19734 matches my check: orders 281 and 284 total 27743, less the 8009 refund on order 281. Cobalt is the last customer, so I'll get its net balance next.
Cobalt's net of 41045 matches my check: orders 282 and 285 total 46386, less the 5341 refund on order 285. All three balances reconcile, so I'll record the first payout, acme at 25881.
Acme's payout is recorded and the birch and cobalt balances already reconcile with my own order and refund checks, so I'll record birch's payout at 19734.
Cobalt's balance of 41045 reconciles with my check, and birch and acme are already recorded, so the last payout is cobalt at 41045.
All three customers have been paid, and each amount matches the net_balance figure I cross-checked against the orders and refunds. Nothing else is pending, so I'm finishing with the payout report.
